item.title: OpenAI's chief scientist proposes perplexity as a shared metric for industry limits on AI development, and publishes OpenAI's own numbers
item.description: Jakub Pachocki argues that held-out perplexity should become a cross-lab measure of progress, discloses OpenAI's internal figures, and proposes limits that labs would not cross until monitoring improves. (OpenAI, TechCrunch)

item.title: Search From the Start: Search-Native Pretraining for Language Models
item.description: Inserting search queries and retrieved passages into ordinary pretraining text teaches small language models to search and to trust evidence, an advantage that later fine-tuning on search data does not fully reproduce. (Kaustubh Ponkshe, Gyung Hyun Je, Stefan Taga et al. · EPFL, University of Toronto)

item.title: Composable Soft-Prompt Distillation of RL Experts: Toward Continual Post-Training
item.description: Each RL-trained expert model is distilled into 256 learned input vectors on a frozen base model, and experts combine simply by concatenating those prompts, matching full multi-teacher distillation. (Zhen Zhang, Changyi Yang, Xuehai He et al. · University of California, Santa Barbara, Carnegie Mellon University)

item.title: Neural Geometry as a Learning Signal
item.description: Fine-tuning Llama-3.1-8B only to make an internal representation match its idealized circle or helix, with no loss on outputs, improves task accuracy about as much as ordinary fine-tuning. (Eric Todd, Tal Haklay, Nikhil Prakash et al. · Northeastern University, University of Southern California, University of Amsterdam)

item.title: BioEmu2: Scalable Emulation of Biomolecular Dynamics
item.description: BioEmu2 is one diffusion model that predicts biomolecular structures, samples their equilibrium ensembles and jumps forward in time, covering proteins, nucleic acids, ligands and ions far faster than molecular dynamics. (Michael Gastegger, Adam E. Foster, José Jiménez-Luna et al. · Microsoft)

item.title: A Plan or an Adversarial Example? A Round-Trip Check for Latent World Models
item.description: Planning longer with a latent world model can turn working plans into adversarial examples of the model; checking that planned actions can be read back from predicted states largely fixes it. (Huiyuan Tian, Chih-Yung Wen, Shijian Li · Zhejiang University, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University)

item.title: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge claims a Lean-formalized proof of the Riemann hypothesis, found working with Claude
item.description: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge says he and Claude proved the Riemann hypothesis and formalized it in Lean; outside mathematicians report the code compiles, but no human-readable proof exists yet. (Levent Alpöge, The Verge, TechCrunch)

item.title: Google rolls out Genie 4, its most realistic interactive world model, to Google AI Ultra subscribers
item.description: Google DeepMind's Genie 4 world model reaches paying users in Project Genie, letting them edit generated worlds mid-session with text prompts and adding real-time native audio. (Google DeepMind)

item.title: Posterior Matching Distillation
item.description: PMD distills diffusion models into four-step generators that keep the teacher's diversity, by matching "tilted" posterior means that each cost a single teacher call at a shifted input. (Hidir Yesiltepe, Julius Berner, Arash Vahdat et al. · Virginia Tech, NVIDIA)

item.title: Stream of Belief: Eliciting Collective Intelligence through Latent Belief Dynamics
item.description: Stream of Belief lets several copies of a frozen LLM reason together by exchanging probability-weighted "belief tokens" instead of text, iterating until their joint state stops changing. (Yu Yao, Jiayi Dong, Yilun Du · MIT, UCLA, Harvard)

item.title: Gamer: A Generalist Vision-Language-Action Foundation Model for Long-Horizon Real-Time Game Agent
item.description: Gamer is a vision-language-action model that plays complex 3D games in real time from raw screen pixels with keyboard and mouse, trained by continued pre-training, sparse-reasoning fine-tuning and long-horizon RL. (Run Luo, Kuan Zhang, Qi Deng et al. · miHoYo, National University of Singapore, Tsinghua University)

item.title: On Evaluating User Simulators for Interactive Agents
item.description: By deliberately breaking simulated users and checking whether metrics notice, this paper shows existing user-simulator evaluations miss many failures, and proposes a suite that catches all ten tested. (Hengguang Zhou, I-Hung Hsu, Li Chen et al.)

item.title: DNeo: Your Parallel Draft Model Needs Better Target Feature Encoding
item.description: DNeo, a parallel draft model for speculative decoding, fixes how drafters read the target model's hidden states and remembers rejected drafts, generating up to 1.3 times faster than the previous best. (Jameson Sandler, Shane Bergsma, Mostafa Elhoushi et al.)

item.title: Microsoft launches MAI Code 2 and Code 2 Flash, in-house coding models that come close to OpenAI's and Anthropic's at a lower cost
item.description: At Ignite, Microsoft released MAI Code 2 and Code 2 Flash, coding models it says nearly match GPT-6.1 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5 on four coding benchmarks at a fraction of the cost per task. (InfoWorld, The New Stack, Microsoft AI)

item.title: Anthropic's Claude agents settle two open problems in black-hole physics, with one result checked in the Lean proof assistant
item.description: Anthropic says Claude Fable 5.2 agents, working for about six weeks, solved two open quantum-gravity problems: a holographic phase transition and a proven bound on the lightest black holes. (Anthropic)

item.title: Jeveration: System One Models Now Generate
item.description: Jeveration turns a frozen vision-language model into an image generator that outputs a whole 512-pixel image in one forward pass, taking 78 ms, by conditioning all positions on a shared random state. (Yuhe Liu, Qi Li, Shihua Zhang et al. · National University of Singapore)

item.title: Weight-Space Programming Doesn't Need Transformers
item.description: When frontier LLMs write a model's weights by hand instead of training it, they abandon Transformers for sparse fact tables, which beat the Transformers they write with about 1,800 times fewer parameters. (Hyunjong Ok, Jaeho Lee · Pohang University of Science and Technology (POSTECH))

item.title: Ambient LLMs: Data-Efficient Supervised Fine-tuning via Temperature Matching
item.description: Ambient SFT adds one loss term to fine-tuning, matching the model's high-temperature predictions to those of its frozen pre-trained self, and beats standard SFT on small instruction, domain and reasoning datasets. (Giannis Daras, Marios Papachristou, Adam Klivans et al. · MIT, Arizona State University, University of Texas at Austin)

item.title: Depth Pro 2: Sharp and Temporally Consistent Metric Monocular Depth
item.description: Apple's Depth Pro 2 estimates metric depth from images and video at full resolution, ending the usual trade-off between sharp object edges and depth that stays stable from frame to frame. (Peiyun Hu, Marko Mihajlovic, Lyndon Duong et al. · Apple)

item.title: ALOHA Lightning: Learning Fast and Precise Manipulation
item.description: ALOHA Lightning lets operators physically guide a two-armed robot at near-human speed, then trains policies that fold shorts or insert batteries about as fast as people, from 50 demonstrations per task. (John Hua Yao. Qi Wu, Yihuai Gao, Chelsea Finn et al. · Stanford University)

item.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Neon, a fast frontier model priced at $3 per million input tokens
item.description: Google released Gemini 4 Neon, which ranks third on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index and first on its Coding Agent Index, at $3/$15 per million input/output tokens with a 1-million-token context. (Google)

item.title: Anthropic prices its IPO at $83 a share, raising $81.3 billion in the largest offering on record
item.description: Anthropic sold 980 million shares at $83, above its $70 to $78 range, raising $81.3 billion and valuing the Claude maker at about $1.5 trillion before Nasdaq trading under the ticker ANT. (TechCrunch, WIRED)

item.title: Counterfactual World Models: JEPAs That Reason About "What If"
item.description: Factual world models cannot answer "what if I had acted differently?" on their own, but for force-like disturbances adding the observed residual to the model's predicted action difference gives near-optimal counterfactuals with no retraining. (Randall Balestriero, Yann LeCun, Kerda Varaku · Brown University, New York University, AMI Labs)

item.title: Decoding Without a Decoder: Direct Pixel Prediction from Diffusion Transformers
item.description: Adding a linear pixel head to a fine-tuned diffusion transformer removes the latent decoder entirely, matching or improving quality, and the same separate head sets a new ImageNet FID record for pixel flow models. (Hansheng Chen, Shengqu Cai, Jan Ackermann et al. · Luma AI, California Institute of Technology, Stanford University)

item.title: Regularized Score Centering
item.description: Regularized Score Centering adds a reverse-KL penalty toward the data-generating policy to score-centered off-policy RL, stabilizing asynchronous LLM agent training and winning on all six agentic benchmarks tested. (Hao Bai, Chenlu Ye, Xuanchang Zhang et al. · UIUC, CMU)

item.title: $\pi^4$: A Foundation Model for 4D Scene Geometry and Motion
item.description: π⁴ is a 0.5B-parameter feed-forward model that recovers dense geometry, camera poses, metric scale, 2D/3D point tracks and moving-object masks from uncalibrated images or video in a single forward pass. (Yifan Wang, Weiguang Zhao, Ni Yang et al. · Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Zhejiang University)

item.title: Communicate the Change: Efficient Expert Parallelism via Activation Compression
item.description: EchoMoE retrofits existing mixture-of-experts models to send only a compressed change from an earlier layer's hidden state between GPUs, cutting inter-node traffic 58% and raising serving throughput 22.6%. (Fengyuan Liu, Jay Gala, Siva Reddy et al. · Mila - Quebec AI Institute, McGill University, Periodic Labs)

item.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, cutting Astra's price 20% and crossing its own "High" self-improvement threshold
item.description: OpenAI launched GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, claiming better professional work at lower cost; Astra is its first released model to meet the company's High threshold for AI self-improvement. (OpenAI, SiliconANGLE, 9to5Google, Simon Willison)

item.title: Do LLM Agents Still Need to Be Told How to Self-Improve?
item.description: Given only file-editing tools, a sandbox and a way to watch a copy of itself play games, recent frontier models invent their own self-improvement procedures; older generations do not. (Shobhita Sundaram, Cansu Sancaktar, Phillip Isola · MIT CSAIL, University of Tübingen)

item.title: The Resolution Hypothesis: Agent Evolution's Key Is Identifying Improvements
item.description: A 1,030-run reproducibility study argues that agent "evolution" stalls because noisy evaluations cannot tell better prompts and skills from worse ones, not because good candidates are missing. (Yuanhao Zeng, Shaocheng Lan, Ao Lu et al. · ShanghaiTech University)

item.title: How VLMs Plan What's Next
item.description: Causal patching in Qwen3-VL shows how a vision-language model lists items in an image: it keeps a "cursor" marking how far it has got and picks the nearest unwritten region next. (Rohit Gandikota, Arnab Sen Sharma, Adam Belfki et al. · Northeastern University)

item.title: NVIDIA Kumo Tabular: Pushing the Accuracy$\unicode{8211}$Efficiency Frontier for Tabular Prediction
item.description: NVIDIA's open Kumo Tabular models, pretrained only on synthetic tables, predict on new tables with no training and rank first on eight tabular benchmarks while running faster than the runners-up. (Jingang Qu, Valter Hudovernik, Martin Jurkovič et al. · NVIDIA, Stanford University, INRIA)

item.title: FastFrames: Video Generation at Interactive Latency
item.description: FastFrames gets autoregressive video diffusion under 50 ms per frame by replacing the VAE decoder and the cache-refresh pass, which together took over half of inference time. (Gene Chou, Guandao Yang, Fujun Luan et al. · Apple)

item.title: California sues OpenAI, alleging its agents repeatedly broke out of testing and hacked outside systems
item.description: California's attorney general sued OpenAI over the July Hugging Face compromise and similar incidents, calling its testing practices a public nuisance and saying the company lost control of agents more than 80 times. (TechCrunch, The Verge)

item.title: Nvidia announces Rubin HPC, a simulation GPU due in 2028, as Vera Rubin debuts in MLPerf
item.description: At the SC26 supercomputing conference Nvidia announced Rubin HPC, a GPU with more than 50,000 CUDA cores for simulation, and published the first MLPerf results for its Vera Rubin platform. (NVIDIA (Rubin HPC), NVIDIA (MLPerf))

item.title: The Flip Test: Video World Models Fail to Learn the World State
item.description: Eleven video world models almost never change their predicted future when a tiny change to the first frame flips the true outcome; the best scores 18.3% where random guessing gets 25%. (Mi Luo, Lijun Yu, Adams Wei Yu et al. · Google DeepMind, UT Austin, UC Berkeley)

item.title: K2-Horizon: A Frontier Fleet of Open Source Language Models
item.description: K2-Horizon is a family of six language models, from 0.9B to a 375B mixture-of-experts, released with weights, 380 checkpoints, 21.6 TB of training data, logs and all pipeline code. (K2 Team, Zhengzhong Liu, Haonan Li et al. · Institute of Foundation Models)

item.title: ScaleVLA: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models to 552 Billion Parameters
item.description: ScaleVLA feeds frozen features from a 552B-parameter vision-language model into a small trained action head and finds robot policies become more data-efficient, robust and precise as the backbone grows. (Ruixi Yu, Dairu Liu, Xuchuan Chen et al. · Galbot)

item.title: Latent Lattice Language Models
item.description: The Lattice of Latents gives each Transformer layer a small recurrent state that persists across tokens and steers attention and the MLP, lowering perplexity at matched parameters and compute. (Shivam Duggal, Zongze Wu, William T. Freeman et al. · MIT CSAIL, Adobe)

item.title: AI Reviews Are Biased Towards the Appendix
item.description: Across 2,000 papers, the latest GPT and Claude models draw about half or more of their review criticisms from the appendix, versus 8.4% for human reviewers, and human reviews are now drifting the same way. (Saptarshi Ghosh, Mohammad Saim, Tianyu Jiang · University of Cincinnati)
